findings: Split the flow into a fast synchronous accept path (validate order, persist it durably, return "processing" to the customer) and a fully decoupled asynchronous fulfillment path, so the 5-second UX guarantee never depends on warehouse/shipping latency

Use a durable, horizontally-scalable queue (e.g. Kafka or SQS) as the buffer between order acceptance and fulfillment workers, so a 50x Black Friday burst is absorbed by queue depth rather than causing rejected orders or timeouts

Apply the transactional outbox pattern (write the order row and its 'order accepted' event in one atomic database transaction, then relay to the queue) to eliminate the dual-write race where an order could be persisted but never enqueued, or enqueued but never persisted

Enforce exactly-once acceptance with a unique constraint / conditional write on order ID at persistence time, guaranteeing no order is ever silently dropped or double-inserted even under retried client requests

Make fulfillment workers idempotent via a dedupe/idempotency-key table keyed on order ID, checked before calling the warehouse/shipping system, so consumer retries or duplicate deliveries from the queue can never fulfill the same order twice

Auto-scale the pool of fulfillment consumer workers based on queue depth/backlog rather than pre-provisioning for peak, so cost stays low at normal traffic but capacity elastically absorbs the 50x spike

Give the fulfillment step its own retry policy with exponential backoff plus a dead-letter queue for calls to warehouse/shipping systems, since those calls are explicitly allowed to be slow and to fail transiently

Wrap external warehouse/shipping integrations in a circuit breaker so transient downstream failures degrade gracefully (orders pile up safely in the queue) instead of cascading back into the customer-facing accept path
Replicate the order store and queue across multiple availability zones (and keep write-ahead durability before acknowledging the client) so no order is lost even if a node or AZ fails mid-burst

Drive order status (received -> processing -> fulfilled -> shipped) off the same event stream and expose it via a status table/polling endpoint or push channel, so customers get real-time visibility without the fulfillment step needing to be synchronous

Instrument queue depth, end-to-end processing latency, consumer error rate, and DLQ size as first-class metrics with alerts tied to the 5-second SLA, so on-call can detect and react to burst-induced backlog before customers notice

Build in an operational backpressure/kill-switch on the fulfillment consumer (pause consumption, not intake) so on-call can halt a misbehaving downstream integration without ever stopping order acceptance or losing events, and safely replay/reprocess from the DLQ once resolved

Keep the accept path's write path minimal and stateless-scalable (no synchronous calls to warehouse/shipping) so its own infrastructure cost stays low and its latency stays flat regardless of downstream system health
